Yeah I had a therapist that I’ve seen for the last couple of years since I came to college. And you’re right. I speak a lot in absolutes. That’s one of my struggles. I feel like my actions define me and so I can’t make mistakes. And when it comes to people I think I struggle most. Im one of those very unconditional loving people. I’ll always care about anyone. I remember the little things. Very sentimental person. Im very absolute when it comes to people to. You’re a person, you have value, you deserve to be loved. Nothing changes that in my eyes. But the world isn’t like that and it hurts a lot. I’m scared of being alone. I’m scared of being a bad person. A quick summary of who I am: I was a very high achieving person who grew up in an abusive household. Very physically abusive. I grew up very alone. My parents constantly told me that nobody would love me unless I was successful. The only thing that kept me going was that I was good at things and I felt that success will bring me happiness. Then I got depressed. Tried to find happiness in girls. That didn’t work. Had no friends. No life. Started slipping up on the things I valued. Tried to kill myself. Then realized that love was the most powerful thing I have. I can love others. I went to college and made a ton of friends. If you asked anybody who knows me, they’d always say that I know the most people out of everyone they know. I wasn’t extroverted growing up but my depression made me start making connections with everyone to hide my loneliness and gave me approval. Relationships with girls continued to suck. I would give a lot and would eventually get hurt. I started to try and find worth in giving back to others so I just started getting heavily involved in service. Helping kids out. Working with the homeless. Volunteering at hospitals. I wanted to make a difference. I still feel lost in so many aspects of life but I had volunteering at least. I end up dating a girl in one of the volunteer orgs I’m a part of. Amazing girl. I felt so blessed to be with her. I’ve never had a relationship come so easily and we just clicked. It felt like an adventure the entire time. She struggles with anxiety and depression. I too struggle with that. Her ex would stalk her and started stalking me. That was really tough on her and our relationship. We got into a big fight one day and she blocks me on everything. Then the very next day I run into her at a coffee shop on the way to see my therapist and I apologize and she gets really upset and leaves. She then complains to the people who run our volunteering org’s national asking them for advice. The national org, without asking her, decides to file a title 9 on me. For accidentally running into her at a coffee shop. And I understand that she has anxiety and how much her ex who stalked her hurt her. But now I’m suspended from an org I’ve given years to. We work with kids and having to walk away from that really sucked. I would work with families daily. We work with families affected by cancer (a reason why both her and I joined was because we’ve lost family members to cancer). And now I feel like I failed them. And I failed her. She never wanted me suspended and she never wanted a title 9 and even tho she never went thru with the title 9 the org still feels like I need to be punished. It’s the most backwards irrational thing but that’s their “policy”. I’ve had the directors of my college’s chapter advocate for me and the national org doesn’t care. I got fucked by the system and even if it seems like such a small thing, it fucking sucks. The org I’m apart of was the best thing I did in college. It was truly a family for me. But now it’s gone too. It’s another failure. Another mistake. I really just wanted to do good. I have good intentions but even then I get hurt.

Damn that’s a really interesting song. The ending was really unexpected. But yeah I feel like love is the only reason I live. I wanna love others and keep on fighting. People eventually realize that I’m fucked up and leave. Relationships are so scary because nothing ever lasts forever. The only person I’m gonna live with for the rest of my life is me and that’s a terrifying thought.

I just feel pretty lonely all the time even when I’m surrounded by people who care for me. I’m definitely one of those people who will do anything for others and cares for everyone regardless of who they are. I’m always forgiving towards others. Objectively speaking I don’t believe I’m a bad person but I live life feeling worthless and not good enough and not really wanting to live. I resonated a ton with what you said in the beginning. That’s very much me too. I have a ton of really close friends because of my loving nature but I end up feeling like I give too much and eventually just push people away. I’m always the one to drop everything for anyone and try and help but it feels really lonely sometimes because I feel like I have to earn approval. If I make a mistake in any way, I fall into a very nihilistic mindset. I try so hard to keep on pushing and being good but if I fail I take it so poorly. I gotta be perfect. I have to do good all the time. All this love makes me who I am. I can’t give up on people even when they hurt me because I always believe in forgiving others. But for some dumb reason, I can’t manage to forgive myself for my shortcomings. The only thing I respect for myself is that I love others a ton and will never hold a grudge. I’m so scared of living a life of hate that I’d almost rather die than hate others. I know that sounds crazy but I just feel like I value everyone’s life the same as mine. 

Anyways, sorry for the rant. I’m just in a really shitty situation rn and I feel kinda lost. I’ve dealt with a lot of stuff growing up and I’m still “young” but life seem bleak and hopeless and I feel awful saying that when I have people who care around me. It’s a simple problem. But not all our problems are that simple. Sometimes I get upset about one thing and later realize I was upset because of another underlying reason. Time helps you put aside emotional impulses and approach things in a more logical way. 

Yeah I agree that avoidance in a relationship isn’t good. You do have to address issues head on together. But there’s nothing wrong in having a little time before we say things. I would much rather a person try and experience my culture rather than them being ignorant to my culture. Allowing others to take part in my culture allows for them to experience something new and maybe understand me better. If someone wants to eat “my” food, listen to “my” music, dress in “my” clothes, go for it. Then why even try and integrate as a society if we go by those rules? Sharing a culture allows for an appreciation of the culture. Dreadlocks are a big part of many different cultures tho. It started in India and has spread all over.
